rounds.text: Triliance Polymers Ltd currently trades at an extreme valuation, with a P/E ratio of 92.8x [E1] that significantly outpaces the sector benchmark of 35.68x [E6]. This premium pricing is difficult to justify given that the company’s compounded profit growth has collapsed to -32% over the trailing twelve months [E18], leading the scanX signal engine to flag the stock for decelerating earnings growth [E56]. Furthermore, the company’s capital efficiency is underwhelming, as evidenced by a median return on equity that has struggled at 0% over the last decade [E20] and remains low at 5% over the last year [E23, E57]. The market’s expectations appear detached from reality, as price growth has recently outpaced profit growth by 6% [E47], while the stock sits at a depressed 19% of its 52-week range [E5]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong long-term compounded profit growth of 25% over the last decade [E15] and maintains an ROCE of 5.77% that exceeds the sector benchmark of 2.14% [E10]. Ultimately, the combination of a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] and a P/B ratio of 3.97x—which is nearly double the sector benchmark of 2.12x [E7]—suggests that investors are paying a high price for a business with inconsistent returns and recent negative growth [E18, E52].
